title: Autotune: default batching/caching heuristics + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Nguyen
release_notes: Introduce an autotune pipeline that computes recommended batching & caching defaults, adds production quantization profiles for common model families, and ships a unit-economics calculator in the console and API. Backwards-compatible: existing configs remain valid; new defaults apply when customers opt into autotune or update defaults.
description: Context: We need to reduce per-token unit cost across hosted and dedicated deployments by surfacing and applying safe defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, and by deploying vetted quantization profiles for common model families. This PR implements an autotune pipeline that computes workload-aware defaults, a small runtime hook to apply recommended batching/caching settings, a quantization profile registry with lookup rules, and a lightweight unit-econ service + console UI for teams to preview expected savings. Motivation: Many teams leave batching and cache disabled or misconfigured; quantization is available but fragmented across models and hardware. Autotune bridges observability -> recommendation -> safe apply, enabling measurable cost reductions with guardrails. Changes (high level): added autotune policy engine and scheduler; heuristics to derive batch_target_ms and prefetch_kv_cache thresholds; quant profiles for gpt-like and llama-like families with CPU/GPU/AMP variants; unit-econ calculator service and API + console UI; added e2e and perf harness tests. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-4821) [x] unit + integration tests [x] perf regression guard [x] docs + console wiring [x] staged rollout plan. Commit summary, changed files, CI and review notes are in metadata fields below.

Ava Nguyen: Added guardrails section to docs; autotune only applies changes when 1) expected cost reduction > 1.5% and 2) 99th-latency impact < 5% relative to baseline, with a canary rollout by default.
Priya Shah: Please add unit tests that validate merge behavior when customer overrides defaults in config and when headroom is low. Also verify quant profile selection for mixed-architecture fleets.
Ava Nguyen: Added unit tests for config merge and expanded integration test to include mixed CPU/GPU scenarios. See tests/perf and server/autotune tests.

notes_on_testing: Perf summary: standard-chat (seq 1024): median token cost -3.8% after batching + q4_0 quant on A100; p99 latency +0.9%.
Stress: Autoscale and batching concurrency validated at 2x baseline load; no KV cache thrashing observed with prefetch_kv thresholds in defaults.yaml.

Rollback plan: runtime exposes autotune.rollout state; disabling the feature reverts to previous config within 30s for in-flight decisions; canary percentage adjustable via Console.
